registers.name: SPH
registers.title: Stack Pointer Registers
notes: Initial value of bits 1:0 printed as RAMEND.

fields.name: SP[9:8]
fields.text: Stack Pointer bits 9:8: address of the stack top. The stack grows from higher toward lower addresses, so a PUSH decrements it. The program must set up the stack space in data SRAM before calling a subroutine or enabling interrupts.

registers.name: SPL
registers.title: Stack Pointer Registers
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as RAMEND.

fields.name: SP
fields.text: Stack Pointer bits 7:0: address of the stack top. The stack grows from higher toward lower addresses, so a PUSH decrements it. The program must set up the stack space in data SRAM before calling a subroutine or enabling interrupts.

fields.name: I
fields.text: Global interrupt enable: no interrupt runs while it is 0, whatever the individual enables say; with it 1, each interrupt follows its own enable bit. Hardware clears it when an interrupt is taken and RETI sets it again; SEI and CLI set and clear it.

fields.name: T
fields.text: Bit copy storage: BST copies a register bit into T, and BLD copies T into a register bit.

fields.name: H
fields.text: Half carry flag: set by a half carry in some arithmetic operations; used for BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Sign bit: always N exclusive-or V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Two’s complement overflow flag, for two’s complement arithmetic.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Negative flag: set when an arithmetic or logic result is negative.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Zero flag: set when an arithmetic or logic result is zero.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Carry flag: set when an arithmetic or logic operation carries.

registers.name: EEARH
registers.title: EEPROM Address Register
notes: The maker prints no address for it: its diagram, drawn with EEARL, leaves it out, and the register summary does not list it.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: EEPROM byte address, linear over the 64-byte EEPROM (0 to 63). Undefined at reset, so write it before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: EEPROM data: the byte to write to the address in EEAR, or, after a read, the byte read from that address.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: EEPROM programming mode: picks what a write to EEPE does, either an atomic erase-then-write or an erase or a write alone. Writes to EEPM are ignored while EEPE is set. Reset returns it to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is busy programming.

rows: Erase then write, as one atomic operation

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: EEPROM ready interrupt enable: 1 enables the interrupt, which fires while non-volatile memory can accept programming, as long as the SREG I-bit is 1; 0 disables it.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: EEPROM master write enable: while it is 1, writing EEPE to 1 within four clock cycles programs the EEPROM at the selected address; with it 0, EEPE has no effect. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is set.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: EEPROM write strobe: writing 1, with address and data set up and EEMPE written to 1 in the four cycles before, writes EEDR into the EEPROM; without EEMPE nothing is written. Write sequence: wait for EEPE to read 0, wait for SPMCSR.SELFPRGEN to read 0 (not needed if software never writes Flash), set EEAR and EEDR if needed, write EEMPE to 1 with EEPE 0, then write EEPE to 1 within four cycles. An interrupt between those last two steps makes the write fail, and an interrupt routine that touches EEAR or EEDR during another access spoils that access. No EEPROM write can happen while the CPU is writing Flash. Hardware clears EEPE when the write time has passed; the CPU halts for two cycles after EEPE is set.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: EEPROM read strobe: with the address in EEAR, writing 1 reads the byte, which is ready at once; the CPU halts four cycles. A read, or a change of EEAR, cannot happen while a write is in progress, so check EEPE first.

fields.name: GPIOR2
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 2.

fields.name: GPIOR1
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 1.

fields.name: GPIOR0
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 0.

registers.name: CLKPR
registers.title: Clock Prescale Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Clock prescaler change enable: must be written to 1, with every other CLKPR bit written to 0 at the same time, before CLKPS can change. Hardware clears it four cycles later or when CLKPS is written; writing it again inside that window neither extends nor clears it.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Clock prescaler select: the factor dividing the selected clock source down to the system clock, which slows every synchronous peripheral; may be changed at run time. To change it, write CLKPCE 1 with the other bits 0, then within four cycles write the new CLKPS with CLKPCE 0. The CKDIV8 fuse sets the reset value: 0b0000 when unprogrammed, 0b0011 (divide by 8) when programmed, as shipped. Any value can be written whatever the fuse.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Sleep mode select.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep enable: must be 1 for the SLEEP instruction to put the MCU into sleep.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD sleep: when it is active, a SLEEP instruction turns the BOD off for that sleep mode. Set by a timed sequence: write BODS and BODSE both to 1, then within four clock cycles write BODS 1 and BODSE 0. It takes effect three clock cycles after being set, and clears itself three clock cycles after that.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD sleep enable: allows BODS to be set, as part of the timed sequence.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up disable.

fields.name: PRTWI
fields.text: Power reduction TWI: 1 stops the clock to the TWI; re-initialize the TWI after waking it.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter0: 1 shuts the module down; when it is enabled again it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter1: 1 shuts the module down; when it is enabled again it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRSPI
fields.text: Power reduction SPI: 1 stops the clock to the SPI; re-initialize the SPI after waking it. Not to be written to 1 when the debugWIRE on-chip debug system is used.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: Power reduction ADC: 1 shuts the ADC down; disable the ADC first. The analog comparator cannot be used while the ADC is shut down.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Watchdog system reset flag: set by a watchdog reset; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Brown-out reset flag: set by a brown-out reset; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: External reset flag: set by an external reset; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Power-on reset flag: set by a power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0. Reading MCUSR and clearing it early lets the flags show the cause of the next reset.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt flag: set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is set for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when this flag, WDIE and the SREG I-bit are all 1.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 enables the watchdog interrupt. With WDE 0 the watchdog is in interrupt mode and a time-out runs the interrupt. With WDE 1 it works in interrupt-plus-reset mode: a first time-out sets WDIF, running the vector clears WDIE and WDIF and leaves the watchdog in system reset mode, and a second time-out before the interrupt has run resets the system. Keeping that combined mode needs WDIE set again after each interrupt, outside the interrupt routine.

rows: Interrupt first, then system reset mode

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 3: with WDP2:0, sets the watchdog time-out while the watchdog runs. A reserved setting (0b1010 and above) acts as one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Watchdog change enable: must be set to clear WDE or change the prescaler bits, as part of the timed sequence. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog system reset enable. WDRF in MCUSR overrides it: WDE is always set while WDRF is set, so clear WDRF before clearing WDE.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 2: with the other WDP bits, sets the watchdog time-out while the watchdog runs. A reserved setting (0b1010 and above) acts as one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 1: with the other WDP bits, sets the watchdog time-out while the watchdog runs. A reserved setting (0b1010 and above) acts as one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 0: with the other WDP bits, sets the watchdog time-out while the watchdog runs. A reserved setting (0b1010 and above) acts as one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: ISC1
fields.text: Interrupt sense control 1: picks the level or edge on pin INT1 that raises external interrupt 1, which runs when the SREG I-flag and its mask bit are set. INT1 is sampled before edges are detected. For an edge or toggle, pulses longer than one clock period raise the interrupt and shorter ones may not; a low level must last until the current instruction completes.

fields.name: ISC0
fields.text: Interrupt sense control 0: picks the level or edge on pin INT0 that raises external interrupt 0, which runs when the SREG I-flag and its mask bit are set. INT0 is sampled before edges are detected. For an edge or toggle, pulses longer than one clock period raise the interrupt and shorter ones may not; a low level must last until the current instruction completes.

fields.name: INT1
fields.text: External interrupt request 1 enable: with this bit and the I-bit in SREG set, pin INT1 raises an interrupt, on the edge or level set by ISC11:ISC10 in EICRA, even when INT1 is an output. It runs from the INT1 vector.

fields.name: INT0
fields.text: External interrupt request 0 enable: with this bit and the I-bit in SREG set, pin INT0 raises an interrupt, on the edge or level set by ISC01:ISC00 in EICRA, even when INT0 is an output. It runs from the INT0 vector.

fields.name: INTF1
fields.text: External interrupt flag 1: set when an edge or logic change on INT1 raises a request; with the I-bit in SREG and EIMSK.INT1 set, the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1. Held at 0 while INT1 is configured as a level interrupt.

fields.name: INTF0
fields.text: External interrupt flag 0: set when an edge or logic change on INT0 raises a request; with the I-bit in SREG and EIMSK.INT0 set, the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1. Held at 0 while INT0 is configured as a level interrupt.

fields.name: PCIE3
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 3: with this bit and the I-bit in SREG set, a change on any PCINT[27:24] pin enabled in PCMSK3 raises an interrupt, run from the PCI3 vector.

fields.name: PCIE2
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 2: with this bit and the I-bit in SREG set, a change on any PCINT[23:16] pin enabled in PCMSK2 raises an interrupt, run from the PCI2 vector.

fields.name: PCIE1
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 1: with this bit and the I-bit in SREG set, a change on any PCINT[15:8] pin enabled in PCMSK1 raises an interrupt, run from the PCI1 vector.

fields.name: PCIE0
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 0: with this bit and the I-bit in SREG set, a change on any PCINT[7:0] pin enabled in PCMSK0 raises an interrupt, run from the PCI0 vector.

fields.name: PCIF3
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 3: set when any PCINT[27:24] pin changes and raises a request; with the I-bit in SREG and PCICR.PCIE3 set, the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF2
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 2: set when any PCINT[23:16] pin changes and raises a request; with the I-bit in SREG and PCICR.PCIE2 set, the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF1
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 1: set when any PCINT[15:8] pin changes and raises a request; with the I-bit in SREG and PCICR.PCIE1 set, the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF0
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 0: set when any PCINT[7:0] pin changes and raises a request; with the I-bit in SREG and PCICR.PCIE0 set, the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCINT[27:24]
fields.text: Pin change enable mask: a 1 enables the pin change interrupt on the matching PCINT[27:24] pin, provided PCICR.PCIE3 is set; a 0 disables it.

fields.name: PCINT[23:16]
fields.text: Pin change enable mask: a 1 enables the pin change interrupt on the matching PCINT[23:16] pin, provided PCICR.PCIE2 is set; a 0 disables it.

fields.name: PCINT[15:8]
fields.text: Pin change enable mask: a 1 enables the pin change interrupt on the matching PCINT[15:8] pin, provided PCICR.PCIE1 is set; a 0 disables it.

fields.name: PCINT
fields.text: Pin change enable mask: a 1 enables the pin change interrupt on the matching PCINT[7:0] pin, provided PCICR.PCIE0 is set; a 0 disables it.

fields.name: BBMD

fields.name: BBMC

fields.name: BBMA
fields.text: Break-before-make mode enable for port A: 1 puts a tri-state cycle in between when DDRxn is written to make a pin an output.

fields.name: PUDD

fields.name: PUDC
fields.text: Port-wise pull-up disable for port C: 1 turns off the port’s pull-ups even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn select a pull-up ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01). ORed with MCUCR.PUD.

fields.name: PUDB
fields.text: Port-wise pull-up disable for port B: 1 turns off the port’s pull-ups even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn select a pull-up ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01). ORed with MCUCR.PUD.

fields.name: PUDA
fields.text: Port-wise pull-up disable for port A: 1 turns off the port’s pull-ups even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn select a pull-up ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01). ORed with MCUCR.PUD.

fields.name: CTC0
fields.text: Clear timer on compare match mode: picks the counting sequence and the source of TOP, between normal mode and CTC mode.

fields.name: CS0
fields.text: Clock select: the Timer/Counter0 clock source. With an external pin source, edges on T0 clock the counter even when the pin is an output.

values.text: External clock on T0, falling edge.
External clock on T0, rising edge.

fields.name: TCNT0

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 compare match B interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR0.OCF0B is set.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 compare match A interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR0.OCF0A is set.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 overflow interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR0.TOV0 is set.

fields.name: OCF0B

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Timer/Counter0 output compare A match flag: set when the counter matches OCR0A. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when this flag, OCIE0A and the SREG I-bit are all 1.

fields.name: TOV0

fields.name: COM1A
fields.text: Compare output mode for channel A: any nonzero value hands pin OC1A to the compare output in place of normal port function; the pin’s DDR bit must be set for the output driver to work. What each setting does depends on the WGM1[3:0] mode. In fast PWM and in both phase correct PWM modes, OCR1A equal to TOP with COM1A1 set is a special case; in fast PWM the compare match is then ignored and the set or clear happens at TOP.

values.text: Clear OC1A/OC1B on compare match (output low).
Set OC1A/OC1B on compare match (output high).
WGM1[3:0] = 14 or 15: toggle OC1A on compare match, OC1B disconnected. Any other WGM1 mode: OC1A/OC1B disconnected.

fields.name: WGM1
fields.text: Waveform generation mode, low bits: with WGM1[3:2] in TCCR1B, picks the counting sequence, the source of TOP and the waveform: normal, CTC, or one of three PWM modes.

registers.name: TCCR1B
registers.title: Timer/Counter1 Control Register B
notes: The settings of WGM1[3:2] are carried on TCCR1A.WGM1, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: ICNC1
fields.text: Input capture noise canceler: 1 filters the ICP1 input, which then changes only after four equal samples in a row, delaying the capture by four oscillator cycles.

fields.name: ICES1
fields.text: Input capture edge select: 0 captures on a falling edge of ICP1, 1 on a rising edge. A capture copies the counter into ICR1 and sets ICF1, which can raise the input capture interrupt. While ICR1 is used as TOP, ICP1 is disconnected and input capture is off.

fields.name: WGM1[3:2]
fields.text: Waveform generation mode, high bits; with WGM1[1:0] in TCCR1A.

fields.name: CS1
fields.text: Clock select: the Timer/Counter1 clock source. With an external pin source, edges on T1 clock the counter even when the pin is an output.

values.text: External clock on T1, falling edge.
External clock on T1, rising edge.

fields.name: FOC1A
fields.text: Force output compare for channel A: writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, and OC1A changes as COM1A[1:0] sets; no interrupt, and no timer clear in CTC mode with OCR1A as TOP. Active only when WGM1[3:0] selects a non-PWM mode; must be written 0 whenever TCCR1A is written in a PWM mode. Reads as 0.

fields.name: FOC1B
fields.text: Force output compare for channel B: writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, and OC1B changes as COM1B[1:0] sets; no interrupt, and no timer clear in CTC mode with OCR1A as TOP. Active only when WGM1[3:0] selects a non-PWM mode; must be written 0 whenever TCCR1A is written in a PWM mode. Reads as 0.

fields.name: TCNT1[15:8]
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, high byte.

fields.name: TCNT1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, low byte.

fields.name: OCR1A[15:8]
fields.text: Output compare register 1 A, high byte.

fields.name: OCR1A
fields.text: Output compare register 1 A, low byte.

fields.name: OCR1B[15:8]
fields.text: Output compare register 1 B, high byte.

fields.name: OCR1B
fields.text: Output compare register 1 B, low byte.

fields.name: ICR1[15:8]
fields.text: Input capture register 1, high byte.

fields.name: ICR1
fields.text: Input capture register 1, low byte.

fields.name: ICIE1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 input capture interrupt enable: with the I-flag in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.ICF1 is set.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 output compare B match interrupt enable: with the I-flag in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.OCF1B is set.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 output compare A match interrupt enable: with the I-flag in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.OCF1A is set.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 overflow interrupt enable: with the I-flag in SREG set, 1 enables the interrupt, which runs when TIFR1.TOV1 is set.

fields.name: ICF1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 input capture flag: set by a capture event on ICP1, or, when WGM1[3:0] uses ICR1 as TOP, when the counter reaches TOP. Cleared when the input capture vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 output compare B match flag: set in the timer clock cycle after TCNT1 matches OCR1B; a FOC1B strobe does not set it. Cleared when the vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 output compare A match flag: set in the timer clock cycle after TCNT1 matches OCR1A; a FOC1A strobe does not set it. Cleared when the vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 overflow flag: when it sets depends on WGM1[3:0]; in normal and CTC modes, on a timer overflow. Cleared when the overflow vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/Counter synchronization mode: while 1, the value written to PSRSYNC is held, keeping the prescaler in reset so the timers stay halted and can be set up together. Writing 0 makes hardware clear PSRSYNC, and the timers start counting together.

fields.name: PSRSYNC
fields.text: Prescaler reset: 1 resets the prescaler shared by Timer/Counter1 and Timer/Counter0, affecting both. Hardware clears it at once unless TSM is set.

fields.name: SPIE
fields.text: SPI interrupt enable: the SPI interrupt runs when SPSR.SPIF is set and the global interrupt enable in SREG is set.

fields.name: SPE
fields.text: SPI enable: must be 1 for any SPI operation.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Data order: 1 sends the LSB first, 0 the MSB first.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: Master/slave select: 1 for master, 0 for slave. In master mode, SS set as an input and driven low clears MSTR and sets SPSR.SPIF; MSTR must then be set again for master mode.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Clock polarity: 1 makes SCK high when idle, 0 low when idle.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Clock phase: chooses whether data is sampled on the first (leading) or the last (trailing) SCK edge.

fields.name: SPR
fields.text: SPI clock rate select: with SPSR.SPI2X, sets the SCK rate as a fraction of fosc in master mode; no effect in slave mode.

registers.name: SPSR
registers.title: SPI Status Register
notes: The settings of SPI2X are carried on SPCR.SPR, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: SPIF
fields.text: SPI interrupt flag: set when a transfer completes, and also in master mode when SS is an input driven low; raises an interrupt if SPCR.SPIE and global interrupts are enabled. Cleared by hardware when the vector runs, or by reading SPSR with SPIF set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: WCOL
fields.text: Write collision flag: set when SPDR is written during a transfer. Cleared, with SPIF, by reading SPSR with WCOL set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: SPI2X
fields.text: Double SPI speed: 1 doubles the SCK frequency in master mode, so the shortest SCK period is two CPU clock periods. As a slave, the SPI is guaranteed only at fosc/4 or lower.

fields.name: SPDR
fields.text: SPI data register.

fields.name: TWBR
fields.text: Bit rate register: the division factor of the bit rate generator that makes SCL in master modes. Must be 10 or more in master mode.

fields.name: TWINT
fields.text: TWI interrupt flag: set by hardware when the TWI finishes a job and waits for software; with the I-bit in SREG and TWIE set, the MCU jumps to the TWI vector. SCL low is stretched while it is set. Cleared only by software writing 1, not by running the vector; clearing it starts the TWI, so finish with TWAR, TWSR and TWDR first.

fields.name: TWEA
fields.text: TWI enable acknowledge: when 1, an ACK is sent on receiving the device’s own slave address, a general call with TWAR.TWGCE set, or a data byte in master receiver or slave receiver mode. Writing 0 takes the device off the bus for a while; writing 1 resumes address recognition.

fields.name: TWSTA
fields.text: TWI START condition: write 1 to become bus master. The TWI sends a START when the bus is free, or waits for a STOP and then sends one. Software must clear it after the START has gone out.

fields.name: TWSTO
fields.text: TWI STOP condition: in master mode, 1 sends a STOP and clears itself when done. In slave mode, 1 sends no STOP but returns the TWI to unaddressed slave mode and releases SCL and SDA to high impedance, to recover from an error.

fields.name: TWWC
fields.text: TWI write collision flag: set by a write to TWDR while TWINT is low; cleared by writing TWDR while TWINT is high.

fields.name: TWEN
fields.text: TWI enable: 1 starts the TWI, which takes over the SCL and SDA pins and turns on their slew-rate limiters and spike filters. 0 switches the TWI off and ends any transfer at once.

fields.name: TWIE
fields.text: TWI interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 requests the TWI interrupt for as long as TWINT is high.

fields.name: TWS
fields.text: TWI status: the 5-bit state of the TWI logic and the bus. A read of TWSR also returns the prescaler bits, so mask those to 0 when testing the status.

fields.name: TWPS
fields.text: TWI prescaler: readable and writable; sets the bit rate prescaler used in the bit rate calculation.

fields.name: TWD
fields.text: TWI data: the next byte to send, or the last byte received.

fields.name: TWA
fields.text: TWI slave address: the 7-bit address of the TWI unit.

fields.name: TWGCE
fields.text: TWI general call recognition enable: 1 makes the TWI recognize a general call on the bus.

fields.name: TWAM
fields.text: TWI address mask: a 7-bit mask over the slave address in TWAR. A bit set to 1 makes the address match skip the comparison of that incoming address bit with its TWAR bit.

fields.name: TWHS
fields.text: TWI high speed enable: 1 clocks the TWI from the undivided system clock. This mode needs clkTWIHS at exactly twice clkI/O, so the I/O clock must be scaled down by 2 (for example, the 8 MHz internal oscillator prescaled to 4 MHz).

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Analog comparator multiplexer enable: 1 while the ADC is off (ADCSRA.ADEN = 0) lets the ADC multiplexer pick the comparator’s negative input; 0 puts AIN1 on the negative input.

fields.name: ADTS2
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 2.

fields.name: ADTS1
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 1.

fields.name: ADTS0
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 0.

registers.name: ACSR
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: Analog comparator disable: 1 switches the comparator’s power off, lowering consumption in active and idle mode; may be set at any time. Clear ACIE before changing it, or an interrupt can occur.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: Analog comparator bandgap select: 1 puts the fixed internal bandgap reference on the positive input in place of AIN0; 0 puts AIN0 there.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Analog comparator output, synchronized, with a delay of 1 to 2 clock cycles.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Analog comparator interrupt flag: hardware sets it when the comparator output does what ACIS1:ACIS0 select. The interrupt runs when ACIE and the SREG I-bit are both 1. Cleared by hardware when the vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: Analog comparator interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 enables the comparator interrupt; 0 disables it.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: Analog comparator input capture enable: 1 connects the comparator output straight to the Timer/Counter1 input capture front end, using its noise canceler and edge select; 0 leaves them unconnected. TIMSK1.ICIE1 must be set for the comparator to raise the input capture interrupt.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Analog comparator interrupt mode select: which comparator events raise the interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing it, or an interrupt can occur.

fields.name: AIN1D
fields.text: AIN1 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: AIN0D
fields.text: AIN0 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: REFS0
fields.text: Reference selection: the ADC voltage reference. A change during a conversion takes effect when that conversion completes (ADCSRA.ADIF set).

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: ADC left adjust result: 1 left-adjusts the result in the ADC data register, 0 right-adjusts it. Takes effect at once, even during a conversion.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: Analog channel selection: which analog input feeds the ADC; channel ADC8 is the temperature measurement. A change during a conversion takes effect when that conversion completes (ADCSRA.ADIF set). After switching to the internal voltage reference, the ADC needs 1 ms to settle, enabled, before measurements are stable.

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: ADC enable: 1 turns the ADC on, 0 turns it off; turning it off during a conversion ends that conversion.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: ADC start conversion: write 1 to start each conversion in single conversion mode, or the first in free running mode. The first conversion after the ADC is enabled takes 25 ADC clock cycles instead of 13, and initializes the ADC. Reads 1 while a conversion runs and 0 when done; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: ADC auto trigger enable: 1 makes the ADC start a conversion on each rising edge of the trigger signal chosen by ADCSRB.ADTS.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: ADC interrupt flag: set once a conversion is done and the result registers hold it. The conversion complete interrupt runs when ADIE and the SREG I-bit are both 1. Cleared by hardware when the vector runs, or by writing 1. A read-modify-write of ADCSRA, SBI and CBI included, can lose a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: ADC interrupt enable: with the I-bit in SREG set, 1 enables the conversion complete interrupt.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: ADC prescaler select: the division factor from the system clock to the ADC clock.

fields.name: ADC9
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 9.

fields.name: ADC8
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 8.

fields.name: ADC9
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 9. With the result left-adjusted, reading ADCH alone gives the result to 8 bits.

fields.name: ADC8
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 8.

fields.name: ADC7
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 7.

fields.name: ADC6
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 6.

fields.name: ADC5
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 5.

fields.name: ADC4
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 4.

fields.name: ADC3
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 3.

fields.name: ADC2
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 2.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 7.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 6.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 5.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 4.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 3.

fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 2.

fields.name: ADC1
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 1.

fields.name: ADC0
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 0. Once ADCL is read, the data registers do not update until ADCH is read, so the full result is read ADCL first, then ADCH.

fields.name: ADC1

fields.name: ADC0
fields.text: ADC conversion result bit 0. Once ADCL is read, the data registers do not update until ADCH is read, so the full result is read ADCL first, then ADCH.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Analog comparator multiplexer enable.

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source: with ADCSRA.ADATE set, picks the source whose interrupt flag rising edge starts a conversion; with ADATE clear it has no effect. Switching from a cleared source to a set one makes a rising edge, which starts a conversion if ADCSRA.ADEN is set. Switching to free running mode (0) makes no trigger even when ADIF is set.

fields.name: ADC7D
fields.text: ADC7 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC6D
fields.text: ADC6 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC5D
fields.text: ADC5 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC4D
fields.text: ADC4 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC3D
fields.text: ADC3 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC2D
fields.text: ADC2 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC1D
fields.text: ADC1 digital input disable: 1 turns off the pin’s digital input buffer, and its PIN register bit then reads 0. Setting it on a pin used only as an analog input saves power in the buffer.

fields.name: ADC0D

fields.name: DWDR
fields.text: debugWIRE data register.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Read-while-write section busy: present for compatibility with parts that have read-while-write; always reads 0 here.

fields.name: CTPB
fields.text: Clear temporary page buffer: writing it while the buffer is being filled empties the buffer, losing its data.

fields.name: RFLB
fields.text: Read fuse and lock bits: an LPM issued no more than three cycles after setting RFLB and SELFPRGEN loads the lock bits or the fuse bits, chosen by Z0 of the Z-pointer, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Page write: written to 1 together with SELFPRGEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles write the temporary buffer to the page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the write completes or if no SPM follows within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole page write.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Page erase: written to 1 together with SELFPRGEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles erase the page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the erase completes or if no SPM follows within four cycles. The CPU halts during the operation.

fields.name: SELFPRGEN
fields.text: Self programming enable: enables SPM for the next four clock cycles. Written with CTPB, RFLB, PGWRT or PGERS, the next SPM does that operation; written alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, ignoring the Z LSB. Clears itself when the SPM completes or if none comes within four cycles; stays 1 until a page erase or page write finishes. Any value of the low five bits other than 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 has no effect.
